5	# build logic itself lives in setup.sh, scripts/build_*.sh, and the Makefiles.
6	#
7	# Usage:
8	#   scripts/build_all.sh [TARGET] [--dry-run]
9	#
10	# TARGET (default: all):
11	#   all       setup.sh (locate external qemu + vsim + plugin) then
12	#             fixtures (the fixtures Makefile also builds the runtime lib too)
13	#             then vlinux
14	#   plugin    qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so
15	#   fixtures  tests/fixtures/*.elf (+ runtime lib)
16	#   runtime   build/runtime/ (rv64) + build/runtime/rv32/ (rv32, when
17	#             HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32 is set): libandesim_runtime.a, crt0.o,
18	#             andesim.ld, andesim.specs, include/andesim/ROI.h
19	#   vlinux    build/runtime/linux/vlinux.elf (the vlinux proxy-kernel
20	#             skeleton, ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md; depends on the runtime
21	#             lib, built automatically)
22	#
23	# --dry-run prints the underlying commands without running them.
24	#
25	# The andesim driver itself is NOT built here: ./andesim self-bootstraps via
26	# scripts/build_driver.sh on first use.
27	set -euo pipefail
28	
29	ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
30	
31	TARGET=all
32	DRY_RUN=0
33	for arg in "$@"; do
34	  case "$arg" in
35	    --dry-run) DRY_RUN=1 ;;
36	    all|plugin|fixtures|runtime|vlinux) TARGET="$arg" ;;
37	    *)
38	      echo "build_all.sh: unknown argument: $arg" >&2
39	      echo "usage: build_all.sh [all|plugin|fixtures|runtime|vlinux] [--dry-run]" >&2
40	      exit 2

53	  "$@"

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# Build the user-facing andesim runtime (runtime/) for both arches. Produces:
3	#   build/runtime/       libandesim_runtime.a, crt0.o, andesim.ld, andesim.specs,
4	#                        include/andesim/ROI.h   (rv64; link -B build/runtime)
5	#   build/runtime/rv32/  the same, rv32          (rv32; link -B build/runtime/rv32)
6	# Users link with `-B <dir> -specs=andesim.specs` (USER_GUIDE.md section 4).
7	#
8	# rv64 always builds (HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN). rv32 builds too when HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32
9	# is set. Self-contained: fills either toolchain from config.env (exported env
10	# wins), like setup.sh, so it runs without `source ./setup.sh` first.
11	set -euo pipefail
12	
13	ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
14	SRC="$ROOT/runtime"
15	CONFIG_FILE="$ROOT/config.env"
16	CONFIG_TEMPLATE="$ROOT/config.env.example"
17	
18	[[ -f "$SRC/Makefile" ]] || { echo "missing $SRC/Makefile" >&2; exit 1; }
19	
20	# Capture exported values (they win), then source config.env to fill any gaps.
21	ENV_TC64="${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:-}"
22	ENV_TC32="${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32:-}"
23	if [[ -z "$ENV_TC64" || -z "$ENV_TC32" ]]; then
24	  if [[ ! -f "$CONFIG_FILE" ]]; then
25	    [[ -f "$CONFIG_TEMPLATE" ]] \
26	      || { echo "missing $CONFIG_TEMPLATE; cannot create $CONFIG_FILE" >&2; exit 1; }
27	    cp "$CONFIG_TEMPLATE" "$CONFIG_FILE"
28	    echo "created $CONFIG_FILE from template -- edit it if your toolchains live elsewhere" >&2
29	  fi
30	  # shellcheck source=/dev/null
31	  . "$CONFIG_FILE"
32	fi
33	[[ -n "$ENV_TC64" ]] && HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN="$ENV_TC64"
34	[[ -n "$ENV_TC32" ]] && HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32="$ENV_TC32"
35	
36	# rv64 (required).
37	if [[ -z "${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:-}" || ! -d "${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:-}/bin" ]]; then
38	  echo "HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN unset or has no bin/; check $CONFIG_FILE" >&2
39	  exit 1
40	fi
41	make -C "$SRC" ARCH=rv64 TOOLCHAIN="$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN"
42	echo "built: $ROOT/build/runtime/libandesim_runtime.a (rv64)"
43	
44	# rv32 (optional: needs the second toolchain).
45	if [[ -n "${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32:-}" && -d "${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32:-}/bin" ]]; then
46	  make -C "$SRC" ARCH=rv32 TOOLCHAIN="$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32"
47	  echo "built: $ROOT/build/runtime/rv32/libandesim_runtime.a (rv32)"
48	else
49	  echo "skipped rv32 runtime: set HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32 in $CONFIG_FILE to build it" >&2
50	fi

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# Run the hybrid e2e tests. Drives tests/*.sh against pre-built artifacts
3	# (source ./setup.sh first to export the external qemu/vsim locations).
4	#
5	# Env overrides:
6	#   VSIM_QEMU    qemu-system-riscv64 (default: $QEMU_BIN_DIR/qemu-system-riscv64)
7	#   VSIM_PLUGIN  libhybrid_handoff.so (default: qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so)
8	#   VSIM_BIN     sim_<cpu> (default: first sim_* under $VSIM_BIN_DIR)
9	#   FILTER       regex; only run tests whose name matches
10	#   MODE         marker | pc | both  (default: both) - drives TRIGGER_MODE
11	#                for round-trip fixtures. Negative drivers run once
12	#                regardless because they assert orchestrator failure
13	#                modes orthogonal to the trigger mechanism.
14	#   JOBS         parallel job slots (default: min($(nproc),
15	#                free(/dev/shm)/256MB)). Each Tier-2 slot uses a 128 MB
16	#                /dev/shm mmap and runs 2 processes (qemu1, vsim); the
17	#                headroom check leaves margin for that plus QEMU's own
18	#                scratch. Pass JOBS=1 for sequential semantics.
19	#   LOG_DIR      where per-test logs land (default: mktemp -d under /tmp)
20	
21	set -euo pipefail
22	
23	ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
24	# vsim sim_* live in the external VSIM_BIN_DIR (setup.sh exports it, mirroring
25	# VSIM_QEMU); empty when setup.sh has not run -- the require below reports it.
26	VSIM_BUILD="${VSIM_BIN_DIR:-}"
27	HARNESS="$ROOT/tests"
28	TEST_DIR="$ROOT/tests/fixtures"
29	
30	VSIM_QEMU="${VSIM_QEMU:-${QEMU_BIN_DIR:-}/qemu-system-riscv64}"
31	VSIM_PLUGIN="${VSIM_PLUGIN:-$ROOT/qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so}"
32	if [[ -z "${VSIM_BIN:-}" ]]; then
33	  # Default to the repo's canonical SINGLE-HART engine (the same one ./andesim
34	  # pins). The fixtures are single-hart programs: on a multicore build like
35	  # sim_ax45mpv_mp2 -- which sorts FIRST under $VSIM_BIN_DIR -- the
36	  # secondary hart runs crt0 from reset, writes SKIPPED to SimControl and
37	  # stops the sim before hart 0 drains, failing every C fixture. Fall back
38	  # to the first sim_* only when the canonical engine is not built.
39	  VSIM_BIN="$VSIM_BUILD/sim_ax45mpv_premium"
40	  if [[ ! -x "$VSIM_BIN" ]]; then
41	    VSIM_BIN=$(ls "$VSIM_BUILD"/sim_* 2>/dev/null | head -n1 || true)
42	  fi
43	fi
44	
45	step() { printf '\033[1;34m==>\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
46	ok()   { printf '\033[1;32m[ok]\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
47	warn() { printf '\033[1;33m[skip]\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
48	fail() { printf '\033[1;31m[FAIL]\033[0m %s\n' "$*" >&2; }
49	
50	require() {
51	  if [[ -z "$2" || ! -e "$2" ]]; then
52	    fail "$1 not found: $2"
53	    fail "build artifacts first: 'source ./setup.sh'"
54	    exit 1
55	  fi
56	}
57	require VSIM_QEMU   "$VSIM_QEMU"
58	require VSIM_PLUGIN "$VSIM_PLUGIN"
59	require VSIM_BIN    "$VSIM_BIN"
60	
61	export VSIM_QEMU VSIM_PLUGIN VSIM_BIN
62	
63	REQUIRED_ELFS=(
64	  handoff_roundtrip rt_pc_jump rt_sign_bits rt_abi_aliases rt_long_roi
65	  rt_all_gprs rt_mem_loadstore rt_unaligned_lh rt_csr_survival rt_shared_mem
66	  rt_priv_smode rt_priv_umode
67	  rt_c_hello rt_c_printf rt_c_matmul rt_c_fcsr rt_c_v_regs rt_c_v_csrs
68	  rt_c_v_matmul rt_c_v_fill
69	)
70	need_build=0
71	for f in "${REQUIRED_ELFS[@]}"; do
72	  [[ -e "$TEST_DIR/$f.elf" ]] || need_build=1
73	done
74	if (( need_build )); then
75	  step "building test ELFs in $TEST_DIR"
76	  make -C "$TEST_DIR" -j
77	fi
78	
79	# Round-trip fixtures: name|fixture-env-prefix. All run on the unified
80	# e2e.sh harness (shared /dev/shm mmap). The TRIGGER_MODE env is
81	# injected per iteration based on $MODE. Negative drivers live in
82	# NEG_TESTS and run once regardless of mode.
83	RT_TESTS=(
84	  "handoff_roundtrip|FIXTURE=handoff_roundtrip"
85	  "rt_pc_jump|FIXTURE=rt_pc_jump"
86	  "rt_sign_bits|FIXTURE=rt_sign_bits"
87	  "rt_abi_aliases|FIXTURE=rt_abi_aliases"
88	  "rt_long_roi|FIXTURE=rt_long_roi"
89	  "rt_all_gprs|FIXTURE=rt_all_gprs"
90	  "rt_mem_loadstore|FIXTURE=rt_mem_loadstore"
91	  "rt_unaligned_lh|FIXTURE=rt_unaligned_lh"
92	  "rt_csr_survival|FIXTURE=rt_csr_survival"
93	  "rt_m_ext_counters|FIXTURE=rt_m_ext_counters"
94	  "rt_m_ext_trigcause|FIXTURE=rt_m_ext_trigcause"
95	  "rt_shared_mem|FIXTURE=rt_shared_mem"
96	  "rt_c_hello|FIXTURE=rt_c_hello"
97	  "rt_c_printf|FIXTURE=rt_c_printf"
98	  "rt_c_matmul|FIXTURE=rt_c_matmul TIMEOUT=120"
99	  "rt_c_fcsr|FIXTURE=rt_c_fcsr"
100	  "rt_c_v_regs|FIXTURE=rt_c_v_regs"
101	  "rt_c_v_csrs|FIXTURE=rt_c_v_csrs"
102	  "rt_c_v_matmul|FIXTURE=rt_c_v_matmul TIMEOUT=120"
103	  "rt_c_v_fill|FIXTURE=rt_c_v_fill"
104	  "rt_c_static_buf|FIXTURE=rt_c_static_buf"
105	  "rt_c_dlm_data|FIXTURE=rt_c_dlm_data CHECK_VSIM_STDOUT=DLM_OK CHECK_LM_EXIT_SIDECARS=1 TIMEOUT=120"
106	  "rt_c_ilm_code|FIXTURE=rt_c_ilm_code CHECK_VSIM_STDOUT=ILM_OK CHECK_LM_EXIT_SIDECARS=1"
107	  "rt_c_hvm_data|FIXTURE=rt_c_hvm_data CHECK_VSIM_STDOUT=HVM_OK CHECK_LM_EXIT_SIDECARS=1 TIMEOUT=120"
108	)
109	
110	NEG_TESTS=(
111	  "rt_corrupt_state|bash $HARNESS/drivers/rt_corrupt_state.sh"
112	  "rt_lm_transport_off|bash $HARNESS/drivers/rt_lm_transport_off.sh"
113	  "rt_hvm_transport_off|bash $HARNESS/drivers/rt_hvm_transport_off.sh"
114	)
115	
116	# Heavyweight round-trip fixtures, run SEQUENTIALLY after the parallel
117	# pool drains. The L6 privilege fixtures need an S/U-capable engine pair
118	# (the default ax45mpv_premium RTL is M-mode-only,
119	# NDS_NUM_PRIVILEGE_LEVELS=1), and the only built RV64 one is
120	# ax66_makatau -- whose Verilator binary runs 32 threads. Two of those in
121	# the parallel pool saturate the box and time out BOTH themselves and the
122	# lighter default-engine tests, so they get the machine to themselves.
123	# Same entry format as RT_TESTS; both trigger modes still apply.
124	SERIAL_RT_TESTS=(
125	  "rt_priv_smode|FIXTURE=rt_priv_smode CHECK_PRIV=1 TIMEOUT=300 VSIM_BIN=$VSIM_BUILD/sim_ax66_makatau QEMU_CPU=andes-ax66,vlen=128"
126	  "rt_priv_umode|FIXTURE=rt_priv_umode CHECK_PRIV=0 TIMEOUT=300 VSIM_BIN=$VSIM_BUILD/sim_ax66_makatau QEMU_CPU=andes-ax66,vlen=128"
127	)
128	
129	MODE="${MODE:-both}"
130	case "$MODE" in
131	  marker|pc|both) ;;
132	  *) fail "MODE must be one of marker|pc|both (got: $MODE)"; exit 1 ;;
133	esac
134	
135	default_jobs() {
136	  local n=1 shm_free shm_cap
137	  n=$(nproc 2>/dev/null || echo 1)
138	  if [[ -d /dev/shm ]]; then
139	    shm_free=$(df -m --output=avail /dev/shm 2>/dev/null | tail -n +2 | tr -d ' ')
140	    if [[ "$shm_free" =~ ^[0-9]+$ && "$shm_free" -gt 0 ]]; then
141	      shm_cap=$((shm_free / 256))
142	      (( shm_cap < n && shm_cap >= 1 )) && n=$shm_cap
143	    fi
144	  fi
145	  (( n < 1 )) && n=1
146	  printf '%d\n' "$n"
147	}
148	JOBS="${JOBS:-$(default_jobs)}"
149	[[ "$JOBS" =~ ^[0-9]+$ && "$JOBS" -ge 1 ]] \
150	  || { fail "JOBS must be a positive integer (got: $JOBS)"; exit 1; }
151	
152	FILTER="${FILTER:-}"
153	
154	LOG_DIR="${LOG_DIR:-$(mktemp -d -t e2e-XXXXXX)}"
155	mkdir -p "$LOG_DIR"
156	RESULTS_FILE="$LOG_DIR/results.tsv"
157	LOCK_FILE="$LOG_DIR/lock"
158	: > "$RESULTS_FILE"
159	: > "$LOCK_FILE"
160	
161	# run_one MODE NAME CMD INDEX TOTAL
162	# Captures the test command's stdout+stderr into $LOG_DIR/$mode--$name.log,
163	# emits one atomic progress line, and appends a TSV row to $RESULTS_FILE
164	# (mode<TAB>name<TAB>status<TAB>rc<TAB>elapsed). flock on $LOCK_FILE
165	# serializes the progress write and the results-file append so concurrent
166	# children (introduced by the parallel-execution commit) cannot interleave
167	# their TTY writes or corrupt the tally file.
168	run_one() {
169	  local mode="$1" name="$2" cmd="$3" idx="$4" total="$5"
170	  local log="$LOG_DIR/$mode--$name.log"
171	  local start end elapsed status rc
172	  start=$(date +%s)
173	  set +e
174	  bash -c "$cmd" >"$log" 2>&1
175	  rc=$?
176	  set -e
177	  end=$(date +%s)
178	  elapsed=$((end - start))
179	  case $rc in
180	    0)  status=PASS ;;
181	    77) status=SKIP ;;
182	    *)  status=FAIL ;;
183	  esac
184	  (
185	    flock 9
186	    case "$status" in
187	      PASS) ok   "[$idx/$total] ${name}[${mode}] (${elapsed}s)" ;;
188	      SKIP) warn "[$idx/$total] ${name}[${mode}] (rc=77, ${elapsed}s)" ;;
189	      FAIL) fail "[$idx/$total] ${name}[${mode}] (rc=$rc, ${elapsed}s) -> $log" ;;
190	    esac
191	    printf '%s\t%s\t%s\t%d\t%d\n' \
192	      "$mode" "$name" "$status" "$rc" "$elapsed" >> "$RESULTS_FILE"
193	  ) 9>"$LOCK_FILE"
194	}
195	
196	# Build the workplan: one entry per (mode, name, cmd) tuple. Order
197	# matters: marker-mode tests first, then pc-mode, then negatives (matching
198	# the original sequential layout so logs are streamed in the same order).
199	declare -a WORKPLAN=()
200	for tm in marker pc; do
201	  [[ "$MODE" != "both" && "$MODE" != "$tm" ]] && continue
202	  for entry in "${RT_TESTS[@]}"; do
203	    rt_name="${entry%%|*}"
204	    env_prefix="${entry#*|}"
205	    # B3: anchor the regex so FILTER=rt_csr does not silently also match
206	    # rt_csr_survival. Users who want a substring match pass '.*marker.*'.
207	    [[ -n "$FILTER" && ! "$rt_name" =~ ^$FILTER$ ]] && continue
208	    cmd="TRIGGER_MODE=$tm $env_prefix bash $HARNESS/e2e.sh"
209	    WORKPLAN+=("$tm|$rt_name|$cmd")
210	  done
211	done
212	for entry in "${NEG_TESTS[@]}"; do
213	  neg_name="${entry%%|*}"
214	  neg_cmd="${entry#*|}"
215	  [[ -n "$FILTER" && ! "$neg_name" =~ ^$FILTER$ ]] && continue
216	  WORKPLAN+=("neg|$neg_name|$neg_cmd")
217	done
218	
219	# Serial phase: same (mode, name, cmd) tuples, executed one at a time
220	# after the parallel pool drains (see SERIAL_RT_TESTS above for why).
221	declare -a SERIAL_PLAN=()
222	for tm in marker pc; do
223	  [[ "$MODE" != "both" && "$MODE" != "$tm" ]] && continue
224	  for entry in "${SERIAL_RT_TESTS[@]}"; do
225	    rt_name="${entry%%|*}"
226	    env_prefix="${entry#*|}"
227	    [[ -n "$FILTER" && ! "$rt_name" =~ ^$FILTER$ ]] && continue
228	    cmd="TRIGGER_MODE=$tm $env_prefix bash $HARNESS/e2e.sh"
229	    SERIAL_PLAN+=("$tm|$rt_name|$cmd")
230	  done
231	done
232	
233	TOTAL=$(( ${#WORKPLAN[@]} + ${#SERIAL_PLAN[@]} ))
234	step "logs: $LOG_DIR  jobs: $JOBS  mode: $MODE  tests: $TOTAL"
235	
236	# FIFO-based bounded job pool. Each child reads one token from $SEM_FIFO
237	# before starting and writes one back on exit; only $JOBS tokens exist,
238	# so at most $JOBS children run concurrently. Opening the fifo in
239	# read-write mode (<>) means writes never block the parent. The fifo
240	# inode is unlinked immediately after fd 8 is bound -- the kernel keeps
241	# the pipe alive as long as fd 8 is open.
242	SEM_FIFO="$LOG_DIR/sem.fifo"
243	mkfifo "$SEM_FIFO"
244	exec 8<>"$SEM_FIFO"
245	rm -f "$SEM_FIFO"
246	for ((sem_i=0; sem_i<JOBS; sem_i++)); do
247	  printf '.\n' >&8
248	done
249	
250	i=0
251	for w in "${WORKPLAN[@]}"; do
252	  i=$((i+1))
253	  w_mode="${w%%|*}"
254	  w_rest="${w#*|}"
255	  w_name="${w_rest%%|*}"
256	  w_cmd="${w_rest#*|}"
257	  read -r -u 8 _tok
258	  (
259	    run_one "$w_mode" "$w_name" "$w_cmd" "$i" "$TOTAL"
260	    printf '.\n' >&8
261	  ) &
262	done
263	wait
264	exec 8>&-
265	
266	# Serial phase: each heavyweight test gets the machine to itself.
267	for w in "${SERIAL_PLAN[@]}"; do
268	  i=$((i+1))
269	  w_mode="${w%%|*}"
270	  w_rest="${w#*|}"
271	  w_name="${w_rest%%|*}"
272	  w_cmd="${w_rest#*|}"
273	  run_one "$w_mode" "$w_name" "$w_cmd" "$i" "$TOTAL"
274	done
275	
276	declare -A MODE_PASS=([marker]=0 [pc]=0 [neg]=0)
277	declare -A MODE_FAIL=([marker]=0 [pc]=0 [neg]=0)
278	declare -A MODE_SKIP=([marker]=0 [pc]=0 [neg]=0)
279	declare -a FAILED_NAMES=()
280	while IFS=$'\t' read -r r_mode r_name r_status _r_rc _r_el; do
281	  case "$r_status" in
282	    PASS) MODE_PASS[$r_mode]=$((MODE_PASS[$r_mode]+1)) ;;
283	    SKIP) MODE_SKIP[$r_mode]=$((MODE_SKIP[$r_mode]+1)) ;;
284	    FAIL) MODE_FAIL[$r_mode]=$((MODE_FAIL[$r_mode]+1));
285	          FAILED_NAMES+=("${r_name}[${r_mode}]") ;;
286	  esac
287	done < "$RESULTS_FILE"
288	
289	# Stream failed-test logs in workplan order so the user sees a
290	# deterministic post-run failure dump.
291	for w in "${WORKPLAN[@]}" "${SERIAL_PLAN[@]}"; do
292	  w_mode="${w%%|*}"
293	  w_rest="${w#*|}"
294	  w_name="${w_rest%%|*}"
295	  w_status=$(awk -F'\t' -v m="$w_mode" -v n="$w_name" \
296	                 '$1==m&&$2==n{print $3; exit}' "$RESULTS_FILE")
297	  if [[ "$w_status" == "FAIL" ]]; then
298	    echo
299	    echo "=== FAIL log: ${w_name}[${w_mode}] ==="
300	    cat "$LOG_DIR/$w_mode--$w_name.log"
301	  fi
302	done
303	
304	echo
305	marker_p=${MODE_PASS[marker]} marker_f=${MODE_FAIL[marker]} marker_s=${MODE_SKIP[marker]}
306	pc_p=${MODE_PASS[pc]}   pc_f=${MODE_FAIL[pc]}   pc_s=${MODE_SKIP[pc]}
307	neg_p=${MODE_PASS[neg]} neg_f=${MODE_FAIL[neg]} neg_s=${MODE_SKIP[neg]}
308	total_pass=$((marker_p + pc_p + neg_p))
309	total_fail=$((marker_f + pc_f + neg_f))
310	total_skip=$((marker_s + pc_s + neg_s))
311	step "summary: marker ${marker_p}p/${marker_f}f/${marker_s}s  pc ${pc_p}p/${pc_f}f/${pc_s}s  neg ${neg_p}p/${neg_f}f/${neg_s}s  total ${total_pass} passed, ${total_fail} failed, ${total_skip} skipped"
312	if (( total_fail > 0 )); then
313	  fail "failures: ${FAILED_NAMES[*]}"
314	  exit 1
315	fi

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# test_all.sh -- run the full andesim test surface. This is the entry point that
3	# replaced the former `andesim test` subcommand (which moved out of the binary).
4	#
5	# Phases (all run, in order, unless named explicitly):
6	#   unit      build/driver/andesim-*-test   the C++ driver unit tests
7	#   contract  tests/andes_sim/*.sh          driver feature + parity contracts
8	#   e2e       scripts/run_e2e.sh            hybrid qemu+vsim round-trips
9	#
10	# Usage:
11	#   scripts/test_all.sh [--dry-run] [unit|contract|e2e ...]
12	#
13	# --dry-run prints the plan without executing (and without building). The
14	# contract and e2e phases need built artifacts -- run scripts/build_all.sh
15	# first. FILTER / MODE / JOBS pass through to scripts/run_e2e.sh unchanged.
16	set -uo pipefail
17	
18	ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
19	
20	DRY_RUN=0
21	PHASES=()
22	for arg in "$@"; do
23	  case "$arg" in
24	    --dry-run) DRY_RUN=1 ;;
25	    unit|contract|e2e) PHASES+=("$arg") ;;
26	    *)
27	      echo "test_all.sh: unknown argument: $arg" >&2
28	      echo "usage: test_all.sh [--dry-run] [unit|contract|e2e ...]" >&2
29	      exit 2
30	      ;;
31	  esac
32	done
33	[ "${#PHASES[@]}" -eq 0 ] && PHASES=(unit contract e2e)
34	
35	step() { printf '\033[1;34m==>\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
36	ok()   { printf '\033[1;32m[ok]\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
37	fail() { printf '\033[1;31m[FAIL]\033[0m %s\n' "$*" >&2; }
38	
39	pass=0
40	failed=0
41	declare -a FAILED_NAMES=()
42	
43	# run_case NAME CMD...  -- execute one case, tally it, dump its log on failure.
44	run_case() {
45	  local name="$1"; shift
46	  if [ "$DRY_RUN" = 1 ]; then printf '  %s\n' "$name"; return; fi
47	  local log rc; log=$(mktemp)
48	  "$@" >"$log" 2>&1; rc=$?
49	  if [ "$rc" -eq 0 ]; then
50	    ok "$name"; pass=$((pass + 1))
51	  else
52	    fail "$name (rc=$rc)"; failed=$((failed + 1)); FAILED_NAMES+=("$name")
53	    cat "$log"
54	  fi
55	  rm -f "$log"
56	}
57	
58	run_unit() {
59	  step "[unit] C++ driver unit tests"
60	  if [ "$DRY_RUN" = 1 ]; then
61	    printf '  %s\n' "scripts/build_driver.sh" "build/driver/andesim-*-test (each)"
62	    return
63	  fi
64	  if ! bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >/dev/null; then
65	    fail "[unit] build_driver.sh failed"; failed=$((failed + 1)); return
66	  fi
67	  shopt -s nullglob
68	  local bins=("$ROOT"/build/driver/andesim-*-test)
69	  shopt -u nullglob
70	  if [ "${#bins[@]}" -eq 0 ]; then
71	    fail "[unit] no unit-test binaries under build/driver"; failed=$((failed + 1)); return
72	  fi
73	  local t
74	  for t in "${bins[@]}"; do run_case "[unit] $(basename "$t")" "$t"; done
75	}

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# Run andesim inside the prebuilt Linux runtime image -- the macOS path
3	# (see Dockerfile.runtime; macOS is run-only, builds happen on Linux CI).
4	#
5	# Two rules make the hybrid handoff correct across the podman-machine VM:
6	#   1. The shared mmap stays VM-local: the container's /dev/shm (--shm-size)
7	#      is tier 1, and the host's HSIM_MMAP_DIR is never forwarded -- a host
8	#      path would be a virtiofs mount, where MAP_SHARED is not coherent.
9	#   2. The caller's cwd is bind-mounted at the SAME path, so relative ELF
10	#      arguments and output files behave as if the run were local (plain
11	#      file IO is fine across the boundary; only the mmap is not).
12	set -euo pipefail
13	
14	ENGINE="${ANDESIM_CONTAINER_ENGINE:-}"
15	if [ -z "$ENGINE" ]; then
16	  if command -v podman >/dev/null 2>&1; then ENGINE=podman
17	  elif command -v docker >/dev/null 2>&1; then ENGINE=docker
18	  else
19	    echo "andesim: a macOS run executes inside a Linux VM and needs podman (or docker)" >&2
20	    echo "           install podman and run: podman machine init && podman machine start" >&2
21	    exit 2
22	  fi
23	fi
24	
25	IMAGE="${ANDESIM_IMAGE:-andesim-runtime:latest}"
26	SHM_SIZE="${ANDESIM_SHM_SIZE:-3g}"   # tier 1 ceiling inside the VM
27	ENTRY="${ANDESIM_IMAGE_ENTRY:-/opt/hybrid_sim/andesim}"
28	
29	TTY_ARGS=()
30	if [ -t 0 ] && [ -t 1 ]; then TTY_ARGS=(-it); fi
31	
32	exec "$ENGINE" run --rm "${TTY_ARGS[@]}" \
33	  --shm-size "$SHM_SIZE" \
34	  -v "$PWD:$PWD" \
35	  -w "$PWD" \
36	  "$IMAGE" "$ENTRY" "$@"

1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
2	"""Classify every spec CSR by its hybrid-handoff transport disposition.
3	
4	The OFFLINE mirror of the wire-format transport set. It reads the spec inventory
5	snapshot (tests/andes_csr/csr_inventory.csv, produced by extract_csr_inventory.py)
6	and assigns each CSR a disposition under the supported envelope: bare-metal,
7	single-hart, M-mode or M+U-mode, trap-free ROI.
8	
9	The policy here must match what include/hybrid/state_abi.h actually transports.
10	The guard test (tests/andes_csr/test_csr_coverage_complete.*) cross-checks the
11	two, so a CSR added to the ABI without a matching disposition (or vice versa)
12	fails CI -- the "nothing missed" flywheel.
13	
14	Dispositions:
15	  TRANSPORT_NOW  already carried in hybrid_state_v1
16	  NEW            writable M-mode plain state -- expansion target
17	  NEW_TRIG       debug-trigger CSR (shares the Debug Module; transported guarded)
18	  NEW_UDELTA     U-mode Andes control; transported, exercised only in M+U
19	  CONST_RO       read-only config/info -- engine derives it; nothing to exchange
20	  EXCL_RV32      RV32 high-half shadow -- irrelevant on RV64
21	  EXCL_SIDEFX    read/write has side effects -- not architectural state
22	  EXCL_W1C_HW    write-1-clear, hardware-driven (like mip)
23	  EXCL_INDIRECT  miselect/mireg access mechanism, not a direct register
24	  EXCL_NEXT      U-mode N-extension trap state (trap-free ROI + usually absent)
25	  EXCL_DEBUG     Debug-mode CSR the handoff itself drives
26	  EXCL_MODE      S-mode / Hypervisor -- outside the M / M+U envelope
27	  EXCL_TRAP      detailed trap-cause latch, live only after a trap
28	
29	Usage:
30	  classify_csr_coverage.py <csr_inventory.csv>            # write csr_coverage.csv beside it
31	  classify_csr_coverage.py <csr_inventory.csv> --stdout   # print, do not write
32	"""
33	from __future__ import annotations
34	
35	import csv
36	import sys
37	from pathlib import Path
38	
39	# CSRs already carried in hybrid_state_v1 today (Bucket A). Names as the spec
40	# summary tables print them (range rows kept verbatim, e.g. pmpaddr1~63).
41	TRANSPORT_NOW = {
42	    "mstatus", "mepc", "mtvec", "mcause", "mtval", "mscratch", "medeleg",
43	    "mideleg", "mie", "mip", "mcycle", "minstret", "satp", "fcsr", "frm",

49	    "pmpaddr0", "pmpaddr1~63",
50	    "pmacfg0", "pmacfg2", "pmaaddr0~47",

54	OVERRIDE = {
55	    "misa": "CONST_RO", "tinfo": "CONST_RO", "tdata3": "CONST_RO",
56	    "mintstatus": "EXCL_RO",
57	    # side-effecting: reading or writing performs an action, so the value is not
58	    # state to round-trip.
59	    "mnxti": "EXCL_SIDEFX", "mscratchcsw": "EXCL_SIDEFX",
60	    "mscratchcswl": "EXCL_SIDEFX", "mcctlcommand": "EXCL_SIDEFX",
61	    "mintsel_jal": "EXCL_SIDEFX", "pushmcause": "EXCL_SIDEFX",
62	    "pushmepc": "EXCL_SIDEFX", "pushmxstatus": "EXCL_SIDEFX",
63	    "wfe": "EXCL_SIDEFX", "txevt": "EXCL_SIDEFX", "ucctlcommand": "EXCL_SIDEFX",
64	    "mcounterovf": "EXCL_W1C_HW",
65	    "miselect": "EXCL_INDIRECT", "mireg": "EXCL_INDIRECT",
66	    "mireg2": "EXCL_INDIRECT", "mireg3": "EXCL_INDIRECT",
67	    "mireg4": "EXCL_INDIRECT", "mireg5": "EXCL_INDIRECT",
68	    "mireg6": "EXCL_INDIRECT",

70	    "dscratch1": "EXCL_DEBUG", "scontext": "EXCL_MODE",
71	    # writable M-mode plain state to add (the expansion).
72	    "menvcfg": "NEW", "mseccfg": "NEW", "mnscratch": "NEW", "mnepc": "NEW",
73	    "mncause": "NEW", "mnstatus": "NEW", "mnvec": "NEW", "mrnxvec": "NEW",
74	    "mtvt": "NEW", "mintthresh": "NEW", "mcounteren": "NEW",

77	    "mcountermask_u": "NEW", "mdcause": "NEW", "mslideleg": "NEW",

84	    "pmacfg4": "NEW", "pmacfg6": "NEW", "pmacfg8": "NEW", "pmacfg10": "NEW",

92	RV32_ONLY = {

96	    "pmacfg1", "pmacfg3", "pmacfg5", "pmacfg7", "pmacfg9", "pmacfg11",

100	def classify(addr, priv, name, mode, section):
101	    if name in TRANSPORT_NOW:
102	        return "TRANSPORT_NOW"
103	    if name in OVERRIDE:
104	        return OVERRIDE[name]
105	    if name in RV32_ONLY:
106	        return "EXCL_RV32"
107	    if mode in ("S-std", "S-andes", "H-std"):
108	        return "EXCL_MODE"
109	    if mode == "D-std" or name in ("dexc2dbg", "ddcause"):
110	        return "EXCL_DEBUG"

114	        return "EXCL_NEXT"
115	    if mode == "U-std" and section == "Counter/Timer Registers":
116	        return "CONST_RO"

121	    if not argv:
122	        print(__doc__)
123	        return 2
124	    inv = Path(argv[0])

126	    rows = list(csv.DictReader(inv.open()))
127	    out = [[r["addr"], r["priv"], r["name"], r["mode"], r["section"],

1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
2	"""Extract the CSR inventory snapshot from the AndeStar V5 SPA PDF.
3	
4	Refresh tool for tests/andes_csr/csr_inventory.csv: parses Chapter 5's summary
5	tables (Tables 5-12, "Summary of Control & Status Registers") into one row per
6	CSR -- addr, privilege, name, mode, section. Run this when the spec revision
7	changes, then re-run classify_csr_coverage.py and the guard test.
8	
9	Requires PyMuPDF (`pip install pymupdf`). Not used in CI -- the committed CSV is
10	the checked-in truth the guard test reads; this only regenerates it.
11	
12	Usage:
13	  extract_csr_inventory.py <spec.pdf> [out.csv]   # default out: tests/andes_csr/csr_inventory.csv
14	"""
15	from __future__ import annotations
16	
17	import csv
18	import re
19	import sys
20	from pathlib import Path
21	
22	ADDR_RE = re.compile(r'^0x[0-9A-Fa-f]{3}(~0x[0-9A-Fa-f]{3}|~[0-9A-Fa-f]+)?$')
23	PRIV = {"MRW", "MRO", "MRW1C", "SRW", "SRO", "URW", "URO", "DRW", "DRO",
24	        "HRW", "HRO"}
25	TABLE_MODE = {
26	    "Table 5": "M-std", "Table 6": "M-andes", "Table 7": "D-std",
27	    "Table 8": "S-std", "Table 9": "S-andes", "Table 10": "U-std",
28	    "Table 11": "U-andes", "Table 12": "H-std",
29	}
30	# Bold group sub-headers that appear inside the summary tables.
31	SECTIONS = {
32	    "Machine Information Registers", "Machine Trap Setup", "Machine Trap Handling",
33	    "Machine Conﬁguration", "Machine Protection and Translation",
34	    "Machine Non-Maskable Interrupt Handling", "Counter Related CSRs",
35	    "Debug/Trace Registers", "CLIC Extension CSRs",
36	    "Machine Indirect CSR Access CSRs", "Machine State Management CSRs",
37	    "Conﬁguration Registers", "Crash Debug CSRs", "Memory CSRs",
38	    "Hardware Stack Protection & Recording", "Trap related CSR", "Control CSRs",
39	    "Enhanced CLIC CSRs", "Physical Memory Attribute CSRs",
40	    "Shadow Register CSRs", "Supervisor Trap Setup", "Supervisor Conﬁguration",
41	    "Supervisor Trap Handling", "Supervisor Protection and Translation",
42	    "State Management CSRs", "SPMP CSRs", "Supervisor Trap Related",
43	    "Supervisor Counter Related", "Supervisor Control",
44	    "Counter/Timer Registers", "Floating-Point CSRs", "ZCE CSRs",
45	    "N Extension CSRs", "Hypervisor Trap Setup",
46	    "Virtual supervisor Indirect CSR Access CSRs",
47	}
48	# Table 11 (AndeStar V5 User Mode) prints no sub-headers; relabel its rows.
49	ANDES_USER = {"uitb", "ucode", "uzobctl", "udcause", "ucctlbeginaddr",
50	              "ucctlcommand", "wfe", "sleepvalue", "txevt", "umisc_ctl"}
51	
52	
53	def extract(pdf_path):
54	    import fitz  # PyMuPDF
55	    doc = fitz.open(pdf_path)
56	    text = "".join(p.get_text() for p in doc)
57	    # The summary chapter: from Table 5 to the "Summary of CSR Existence" table.
58	    start = text.index("Table 5: RISC-V Standard Machine Mode CSRs")
59	    # "Summary of CSR Existence" also appears in the TOC (before start); take the
60	    # body occurrence that follows the Table 5 caption.
61	    end = text.index("Summary of CSR Existence", start)
62	    lines = [l.strip() for l in text[start:end].splitlines()]
63	    rows, mode, sec, i = [], "?", "?", 0
64	    while i < len(lines):
65	        l = lines[i]
66	        tm = [k for k in TABLE_MODE if l.startswith(k + ":")]
67	        if tm:
68	            mode = TABLE_MODE[tm[0]]; i += 1; continue
69	        if l in SECTIONS:
70	            sec = l; i += 1; continue
71	        if ADDR_RE.match(l) and i + 1 < len(lines):
72	            p = lines[i + 1]
73	            if p in PRIV or ("/" in p and p.split("/")[0] in PRIV):
74	                name = lines[i + 2] if i + 2 < len(lines) else "?"
75	                s = "Andes User Mode CSRs" if name in ANDES_USER else sec
76	                rows.append([l, p, name, mode, s]); i += 3; continue
77	        i += 1
78	    return rows
79	
80	
81	def main(argv):
82	    if not argv:
83	        print(__doc__)
84	        return 2
85	    pdf = argv[0]
86	    out = Path(argv[1]) if len(argv) > 1 else (
87	        Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
88	        / "tests/andes_csr/csr_inventory.csv")
89	    rows = extract(pdf)
90	    out.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
91	    with out.open("w", newline="") as f:
92	        w = csv.writer(f)
93	        w.writerow(["addr", "priv", "name", "mode", "section"])
94	        w.writerows(rows)
95	    print(f"wrote {out} ({len(rows)} rows)")
96	    return 0

15	hang the DM handshake, so the engine and this checker gate on the same map.

18	cpu_config_to_march_converter (parse_inc / is_yes / _int), so this depends only
19	on the Python stdlib.

35	def parse_inc(path) -> dict:
36	    """{macro: string-value} from a Verilog config.inc (`define KEY VALUE)."""
37	    out: dict = {}
38	    for line in Path(path).read_text(errors="replace").splitlines():
39	        m = _DEFINE_RE.match(line)
40	        if not m:
41	            continue
42	        name = m.group(1)
43	        raw = (m.group(2) or "").strip().rstrip(",")
44	        comment = (m.group(3) or "").strip()
45	        if not raw:                                   # bare `define NAME flag
46	            out.setdefault(name, "1")
47	            continue
48	        if raw.startswith('"') and raw.endswith('"'):  # quoted string
49	            out[name] = raw[1:-1]
50	            continue
51	        c = comment.strip().strip('"')                # numeric + // symbolic
52	        if c and " " not in c:
53	            out[name] = c

55	                int(raw, 0)
56	                out.setdefault(name + "_INT", raw)

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# setup.sh env contract: after `source ./setup.sh`, QEMU_BIN_DIR /
# VSIM_BIN_DIR / VSIM_QEMU / VSIM_PLUGIN must be EXPORTED -- i.e. visible to
# CHILD processes, because that is how they are consumed (`bash
# scripts/run_e2e.sh`, the driver, the test harnesses all read the
# environment).
#
# Regression: QEMU_BIN_DIR/VSIM_BIN_DIR were declared `local` inside
# _hybrid_setup_main and exported later in the same function -- exporting a
# local dies at function return, so the sourcing shell kept only VSIM_QEMU/
# VSIM_PLUGIN (never in the local list). Worse, HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN survived,
# which makes tests/lib/paths.sh skip its config.env fallback: a
# setup.sh-sourced shell was strictly WORSE off than a fresh one, and
# run_e2e.sh silently fell back to the legacy in-tree vsim path.

set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)

# Source in a clean bash, then read the vars from a CHILD of that shell.
out=$(env -u QEMU_BIN_DIR -u VSIM_BIN_DIR -u VSIM_QEMU -u VSIM_PLUGIN \
      bash -c "cd '$ROOT' && source ./setup.sh >/dev/null 2>&1;
               bash -c 'printf \"%s|%s|%s|%s\" \
                 \"\${QEMU_BIN_DIR:-}\" \"\${VSIM_BIN_DIR:-}\" \
                 \"\${VSIM_QEMU:-}\" \"\${VSIM_PLUGIN:-}\"'")
IFS='|' read -r qemu_dir vsim_dir vsim_qemu vsim_plugin <<<"$out"

fail() { echo "FAIL[setup_exports]: $*"; exit 1; }

[ -n "$qemu_dir" ]    || fail "QEMU_BIN_DIR not exported to children"
[ -n "$vsim_dir" ]    || fail "VSIM_BIN_DIR not exported to children"
[ -n "$vsim_qemu" ]   || fail "VSIM_QEMU not exported to children"
[ -n "$vsim_plugin" ] || fail "VSIM_PLUGIN not exported to children"
[ -d "$vsim_dir" ]    || fail "VSIM_BIN_DIR=$vsim_dir is not a directory"

  || fail "no sim_* under exported VSIM_BIN_DIR=$vsim_dir"

echo "PASS[setup_exports]"

findings.title: Header claims 'an exported value in your shell takes precedence' -- false for the setup.sh path
findings.detail: Lines 7-9 say 'Both setup.sh and the test harness scripts load ./config.env at startup, so an exported value in your shell takes precedence; this file fills in the gaps'. That is true for tests/lib/paths.sh (sources config.env only when HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN is unset, lines 17-19) and for scripts/build_runtime.sh (captures exported values first, lines 21-34), but false for setup.sh: it sources config.env unconditionally (setup.sh line 76), and config.env's plain assignments (HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN=..., QEMU_BIN_DIR=..., VSIM_BIN_DIR=...) overwrite any exported value. A user exporting QEMU_BIN_DIR to point at a different QEMU and then running `source ./setup.sh` silently gets the config.env value instead, contrary to this comment. Structural fix: correct the comment to state that setup.sh always takes the config.env values (or scope the precedence claim to the harness scripts). Making setup.sh honor the environment would be a behavioral change and is out of scope here; this pairs with the env-resolution consolidation finding in build_runtime.sh.
